requirements.title: An array designator does not by itself prescribe element reference order
requirements.definition: The appearance of an array designator does not indicate an order in which the elements of the array are referenced, except in contexts where array element ordering is specified by 9.5.3.3. This requirement records only the absence of an ordering implication and the explicit dependency on the array-element-order rules; it does not define subscript order values itself.

pending.no-order-from-designator: PENDING source plan with a rank-one INTEGER array initialized to distinct literals [11,22,33] and an elemental or whole-array expression whose final literal oracle is independent of any element visitation order, plus a source review note that no side-effect oracle is used. Non-vacuous because the elements differ and the expression actually consumes the designator.
pending.array-element-ordering-exception: PENDING source-only cross-owner plan using an array element designator with fixed bounds and subscripts where the only ordering claim is delegated to 9.5.3.3. The independent oracle would be the table-derived subscript order value for constants; non-vacuous because changing one subscript changes the computed ordinal, not an address or compiler traversal.

requirements.oracle: Every facet is a pending source plan. Positive-control plans use independently chosen literal values, SHAPE/SIZE inquiries, or scalar results that first establish definedness and reached execution; diagnostic plans pair an otherwise legal source with a minimal repair and require the reported cause to match the stated grammar or semantic predicate, not an unrelated parse, declaration, unsupported-feature, resource, or runtime failure.
requirements.oracle_limitation: This source-only catalogue creates no Fortran test program, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. Numbered syntax rules and constraints carry the 4.2 detection and reporting duty, but these plans do not require a fixed message, fatal rejection, nonzero status, or printed rule number. Unnumbered prose restrictions are not promoted to numbered-constraint diagnostics; runtime-valued predicates remain runtime/source obligations unless a future review separately establishes a static context.

review_rationale: Independent source review in doc/source_audits/batch_090.json reads the original 9.5.1 paragraph and its two fine units and confirms that it states only that no order of reference to array elements is implied by the appearance of an array designator, except where array element ordering in 9.5.3.3 is specified. The exception is recorded as a dependency on its owner rather than duplicated here, and no evaluation-order guarantee is invented. Both facets remain pending source plans; no case, execution, oracle or fixture approval is created.
